case_name: State of Rajasthan v Ram Narain and Others
facts: On 14-8-1983 when victim Anoop Devi aged between 15 and 17 years was coming from the house of her uncle to her parents' house, these accused enticed her to believe that all the womenfolk had assembled at the outskirts of the village to go to circus and induced her to accompany them.
Innocently believing their statement, she accompanied them to the outskirts but did not find womenfolk there.
She was taken at knife point to another village by the name Siroha and from there to Jaipur in a truck.
From Jaipur, she was wrongfully confined in a house.
From there she was brought back to her village and was confined in the house of the first accused.
On coming to know of it, the father of the victim (PW 3) made a complaint to the police and the police recovered her from the house of the first accused.
issues: Whether the High Court is right in reducing the sentence to the period already undergone, i.e., one and a half months ?
petitioner_arguments: The victim (PW 1) is an innocent village girl.
Her evidence clearly indicates that she was wrongfully confined at different place.
Even after she was brought to the native place she was wrongfully confined in the house of first accused.
respondent_arguments: Looking at the evidence of the victim herself, the High Court was justified in reducing the sentence.
She is a consenting party and without independent corroboration, her evidence would be suspect and could not be relied upon.
court_reasoning: The evidence on record was sufficient to prove that the prosecution has established its case without any room for doubt.
Her evidence brings home the guilt of offences u/ss. 364 and 361 and also wrongful confinement u/s. 342.
As regards offence under Section 376, her evidence is sufficient.
holding: The conviction of the first accused is upheld and he is sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 5 years u/s. 376.
Equally, all the three accused are convicted u/ss. 366 to undergo sentence of five years u/ss. 366 and one year u/ss. 342 IPC.
The fine, if paid, is directed to be paid to the victim.
cases_cited: State of Rajasthan v Ram Narain
